actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the object-start draw; the upstream reset() takes no seed and uses the global random module (panda_env.py:87), so only the fake repeats for a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: seed

facts.text: PandaEnv is registered as panda-v0 with entry point gym_panda.envs:PandaEnv
The action space is a four-element Box with every element between -1 and 1
The observation space is declared as a five-element Box with every element between -1 and 1
A step moves the hand target by action[0], action[1] and action[2] times 0.005
The fourth action element is the position target of finger joints 9 and 10
The hand state is link 11 and the finger state is joints 9 and 10
The observation is the hand position followed by the two finger positions as a float32 array
The episode ends with reward 1 when the object is above z = 0.45, otherwise the reward is 0 and done is false
A step after MAX_EPISODE_LEN ends the episode with reward 0
A reset draws the object start uniformly in x 0.5 to 0.8 and y -0.2 to 0.2 at z = 0.05
A reset sets gravity to -10 and loads the plane, Panda, table and tray in PyBullet
A reset puts the seven arm joints at fixed rest poses and both fingers at 0.08
A step calls PyBullet's stepSimulation once
The constructor opens a PyBullet GUI
render() returns an image with 960 columns and 720 rows
The README's PD example states that PyBullet's default timestep is 240 Hz

determinism.notes: the fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed because it draws the object start from random.Random(seed); the upstream PandaEnv.reset() takes no seed and uses the global random module (panda_env.py:87), so the sim backend, which was not run, does not apply the seed

gaps: PyBullet rigid-body dynamics with contacts: a step calls stepSimulation once (panda_env.py:43) at PyBullet's default 240 Hz (README.md:65) with gravity -10 (panda_env.py:73); the URDF and PyBullet defaults are the actuator, sensor and noise model, and there is no other

the checked fake backend is a kinematic stand-in: it integrates the hand target by action * 0.005, sets the finger joints directly and applies a placeholder grasp rule; it runs no PyBullet, URDF, inverse kinematics, contacts, joint limits or gravity
the fake's hand start pose and grasp radius are placeholders; PyBullet computes the hand pose from the URDF and the rest joint poses (panda_env.py:77-80)

the upstream reset() accepts no seed or options and draws the object start from the global random module (panda_env.py:87); the fake accepts a seed and repeats a seeded trajectory, while the sim backend was not run
the upstream render() returns a 720x960 RGB image (panda_env.py:106-115); the fake has no renderer and cap.world.render.v1 stays unbound
snapshot and restore are not offered: PandaEnv exposes only a private _get_state (panda_env.py:118-119) and no set_state
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware; the upstream opens a PyBullet GUI when constructed (panda_env.py:20)

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
